Messages.Author: Lupus Australis
Messages.Body:
On Fri, 7 May 1999, Robert C Campbell Jr wrote:

> I torporize Ozmo
> I diablarize Ozmo
> Somebody brings another one right out.
>
> ??
>
> I JUST BURNED HIM!! Ozmo shouldn't be allowed to come back. If somebody
> could give me a good explanation as to why Ozmo (or anyone else) can come
> right back out after I've doused his ass, then I'd like to hear it.

Perhaps you are not too familiar with Vampire fiction. How many times has
Dracula been "burned" and still risen from the grave, in all the comics,
books, and movies that deal with him?

In "Interview with the Vampire" did not Louis and Claudia "burn" Lestaat?
Was not the equivalent of a bloodhunt then called on Louis and Claudia?
Was not Claudia burned in this bloodhunt? Did not Lestaat then turn out
*not* to be dead?

Having supposedly dead characters suddenly pop up again in perfectly
within the spirit of all kinds of storytelling, especially in the horror
vein.

To give one possible explanation for your above example: Perhaps you only
thought you attacked and diablerized Ozmo. But Ozmo had arranged another
vampire to take his identity. Ozmo then goes into hiding for a time.

Or, to take another explanation: Suppose Ozmo *is* dead? How does this
prevent another, similar vampire, from later assuming his identity?
Anyone with any imagination could invent a thousand other explanations.

Such explanations are really required only in the case of diablerie, and
perhaps handful of other cases in which "burning" clearly implies the
destruction of a vampire. In most cases, however, "burning" could just as
easily mean a complete loss of Methuselah influence over a particular
vampire. Take "Golconda" for instance: In this case burning the vampire
does not mean his physical destruction, but merely his withdrawal from the
Jyhad from having obtained "inner peace".

> > I torporize Ozmo

> > could give me a good explanation as to why Ozmo (or anyone else) can come
> > right back out after I've doused his ass, then I'd like to hear it.

There have been a lot of flippant (not to say they weren't amusing) answers
to this question. I see more of an interesting rules possibility. I think it
is relatively widely accepted that combat is one of the more difficult
strategies to win tournaments with. It is by no means impossible, but it
requires walking a very tight line - as PDB6 has often said.

What if, when a vampire was burned, it couldn't be influenced back into play?
Just think about it for a moment. Not only do we avoid making strange RPG
conspiracy explanations, we add another possible strength - and consideration
to playing combat decks. I am not suggesting a modification to the core
rules, just that it be consider as another variant rule possiblity.

Why should another methuselah be able to ignore your burning of a central
vamp when you invest so much effort into it? Wouldn't it be much more
interesting if playing an Amaranth/Decapitate had a permanent rather than a
reversable effect

Autarch.

I'm not sure I get your point. Burning a vampire is almost always a
permanent effect. That copy of the card, as well as all the influence and
blood invested in it, are gone permanently.

Of course this does not prevent him from using further influence and pool
resources to bring out another vampire. He has still lost his original
pool investment, regardless of whether his next vampire turns out to be
another copy of the same vampire or not.

It is generally a bad thing to have too many multiples of the same vampire
in your crypt, especially if you get them both on the opening draw.
Unusual and creative deck designs will often risk this disadvantage in
order to ensure that they get the vamp they need, but I see no reason why
such decks should be disproportionately victimized by your proposed rule.

For instance, it is rather sad that, if I want to make a SER-PRO-ANI deck,
I must put 6 copies of Mirembe Kabbada in my crypt. For various reasons,
I'd rather have multiple SER-PRO-ANI vampires to choose from. Why is your
proposed rule needed in order to further penalize non-standart decks?

You are also assuming that the rule will always help the combat deck that
does the burning. This has not been generally true in my experience.
There have been times when I have wanted to bring out a vampire (Duck,
for instance), but could not because someone else had him out already. So
guess what...I head across the table, beat the crap out of Duck, and then
burn his ass. A little later, it turns out that Duck is working for me.
This makes perfect sense to me from a storytelling standpoint. It turns
out that I spared Duck's life after all, and now control him through
terror, having fully demonstrated my ability to take his life at will.

This is the difficulty. Why is it any different than contesting a vampire that
is in play? I know that sometimes contestation can be explained as trying to
ensure the loyalties of a single vampire, but couldn't it also be seen as the
same when a vampire has "faked his death" (by being burned and then
reinfluenced?) - the original methuselah wouldn't be too happy either way.

OK, now this is a real problem. Some of these fringe decks are even harder to
play than pure combat ("this deck only works if I get Marty Lechtansi out" is
the only one I can think of off the top of my head). Need to consider this
difficulty for a variant rule system, in order not to run into problems as
ridiculous as those in the "War Of Ages" rules variants proposed by WotC.

>
> You are also assuming that the rule will always help the combat deck that
> does the burning. This has not been generally true in my experience.
> There have been times when I have wanted to bring out a vampire (Duck,

> This makes perfect sense to me from a storytelling standpoint. It turns
> out that I spared Duck's life after all, and now control him through
> terror, having fully demonstrated my ability to take his life at will.

OK, this makes a good point. COnsidering all of the above, I offer the
following variant rule for consideration:

Ashes to Ashes
Place any vampire that is burnt during gameplay in a central location. All of
these vampires may not be influenced into play. Any methuselah may burn 1 pool
and four transfers during their influence phase to remove a vampire from this
central location.

This way, we can have both the semi-permanent "doused his ass" combat effects
with "good" strange RPG conspiracies to allow vampires to return to play, thus
not permanently crippling "theme" decks. I think you deserved to be reamed if
you play a OTP that can't get over your core vampire being hosed - after all,
who you gonna'call... when you get pentex subversion'd?

Autarch

vampires, for example. They take all the weenies out of the game.

playing. Stealth bleed decks that run around Five copies of Ozmo and Five of
Didi Meyers would become useless, requiring their players to become CREATIVE

My group does use the "burned means burned" rule in friendly games. It doesn't
really affect our games much, since we don't usually have those 8 copies of
so-and-so crypts. Some of our decks do have multiple copies of a vampire if he
just really shines when used in a particular deck, but it does make you lay it

Messages.Author: PDB6
Messages.Body:
Robert wrote:
>>I just think tournament style jyhad is weighted way too heavily in the hands
of the stealth-bleeders and not enough in the hands of the combat decks.
This SLIGHT modification would offer up the possibility that you might get
screwed playing a deck whose only cards are governs, cloaks, and
conditionings.>>

I'm clearly the wrong guy to adress this point to. As it is, well designed and
well played combat decks can do just fine at tournaments--if more people played
them, they'd win more often. They are in no way tourney dominating, but they
are competetive (and eat S+B decks for lunch, I might add...). I assure you
that wheither or not a burned dude stays burned will not help the state of
combat decks in tournaments.

As to this not being errated--the reason it has not been errated is that it is
not neccessary for game balance or to make rules work better. Errata is issued
so that the game mantains balance and to clarify rules. As this issue does not
affect either of this conditions of the game, there is no need to change it.
The game was designed so that burned dudes did not stay burned, and as such,
there is no real good reason to change it.

I understand that one might like the logic of a change like this. I can even
see why. Heck, I can even see how the game might seem more elegant if this had
been the rule from the start. However, it simply is not necessary, and will
damage far more than it fixes (which, as it fixes nothing, is completely
unacceptable).

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:
>Stealth bleed decks that run around Five copies of Ozmo and Five of
>Didi Meyers would become useless, requiring their players to become CREATIVE
>with their vamp draws. The trillion master card Anson deck would grind to a
>halt unless their players planned to actually try to keep Anson alive.

About the "keeping Anson alive" part, that would really ruin the atmosphere of
the game. I have to admit that in my games, I like keeping my vamps alive and
trying not to waste them. But remember, we're supposed to be Methusalehs. We
shouldn't really worry about keeping our vamps alive when they're such
expendable resources. Reminds me of a post a few months ago when someone said
that there should be cards specific to a individual vampire (like a card that
only Anson could use or something). The idea appealed to me but would not be
in the spirit of the game, since the focus of the game is on the STRUGGLE
between Methusalehs, not the vampires that are mere pawns.

Also, I would like to concur with several of the opinions already voiced on
this subject. The concept of "burning" not necessarily being completely
destroying does seem to make some sense as does the concept of "merely losing
influence."

Halcyan 2

I can see how the added dynamic might be "cool", as you say. But I can't
see it as being incorporated into the base rules, or added to DCI tournament
rules. The idea behind sanctioned tournaments is to get a playing field
that isn't dominated by particular cards/combos, yet keeps the base rules to
the game as close as possible, so that non-web surfing players might have a
bit of a chance when they participate. Granted, this job hasn't been done
perfectly, but that seems to be what's being aimed for. Start throwing in
house rules like this, whether they alter the dynamnic favorably towards
combat, or not, and many people are going to be left saying WTF? Rules
changes to date have been based on issues that were seen as crippling
certain aspects of the game. Reinfluencing burned vamps has yet to come up
as an issue to date for anyone I know. I can't see it being argued as a
necessary rules change in order to restore balance to some dynamic of the
game. Thus, I can't see it as being incorporated into the base rules or into
sanctioned tournament play. (I do think its a cute little house rule,
though.)

As an aside, I'd dispute your claim that this will help combat decks.
If the proverbial 5+5 Ozmo/Didi deck were made, I'd be ecstatic with a Rush
combat deck. Under current rules, my prey (5+5) could influence out a max.
of 2 vamps. This gives me plenty of time to address the rest of the table.
Also, if my prey can reinfluence after a vamp is burned, that provides me
with another target to Rush. Effective rush is always a more debilitating
way to attack your prey, when compared to the bleeding capabilities of a
typical Rush deck. If he couldn't reinfluence, thats one less way to damage
him...

Regards,
R. David Zopf
Atom Weaver (& V:EKN Prince of Charlotte, NC)

Okay.

There's an expansion Tremere, I can't think of the name off hand, that can
burn blood for bonus bleed. I'm sure you know of the guy.

Here's what I saw (not naming any names here, but I was at his house last
night.) a friend of mine do with a deck once:

Brings the guy out.
Gives him a fortitude master.
Takes an action to go get the Soul Gem.
Force of Will to directed +2 his prey.
Uses, uhh, daring the dawn (I think that's the card) to make it unblockable.
Burns all the blood off the guy to make it like an eight or nine bleed.
Takes his two ag (one from force of will and one from daring the dawn) and
burns. Soul Gem goes into effect, and guess who comes right back out: The
same vamp.

Because of the skill card, the new copy is one cap lower so it comes strait
back into play after taking its two agg, with the soul gem. (he only has one
vamp in his crypt, just a zillion copies)

Next turn he hunts to become tapped so he can run the same gambit over and
over again. An unblockable bleed for eight or so every turn and the dude
with DOM out to bounce in the mean time. Only has to bring out one vamp, so
he's got plenty of pool sitting around.

Cool idea, huh? Ever seen a better crowbar to the rules? I mean, the deck is
sweet and all, but I still maintain it's cheesey as screw. Cheese beyond
cheese. And would be made ineffective by that slight change in the rules we
were talking about.

Ahem.
Challenge met?

>
> Brings the guy out.

Which takes a minimum of two turns *if* you get an Info Highway or a
Tomb of Ramses out on your first turn (or on your second if you go late
enough in the rotation). Typically takes three turns.

By this time, a good rush deck will be guaranteed a vampire with which
to rush Spiro and clobber him silly. Probably even torporize him. But,
not every deck is a rush deck, so...

> Gives him a fortitude master.
> Takes an action to go get the Soul Gem.

Which should be blocked. Many decks can find +1 intercept by the fourth
turn. Then what? One intercept and this deck is shut down.

> Force of Will to directed +2 his prey.

That's just +1, since he ony has basic Fortitude. But anyway...

> Uses, uhh, daring the dawn (I think that's the card) to make it unblockable.

Unblockable by vampires. But OK (most decks don't have allies out to
block with). But (as an aside) this deck will get shut down hard by
an Arms Dealer deck (or a Garou deck). Your point still stands, though.

> Burns all the blood off the guy to make it like an eight or nine bleed.

Right.
"All the blood" = 8 ('cause he still has to pay one for the FoW).
Total bleed = 1+1(FoW)+6(special) = 8.

So, if you're playing one of the decks that hasn't shut down this deck
already (i.e., not a rush deck and not an intercept deck), what is your
bleed defense? Bounce.
Bounce shuts this deck down, and gets a good boost in oust its own prey
while doing it.

it's a very bad thing. And you know how many Deflections our group
tends to pack... this deck would be terribly entertaining but a risky
play in a tournament. =) Especially when you ran out of Spiridonii.

the same, and you should know better than most of us how much fun that
is.
